items.title: Find your next favourite local business at Sourced in Sauga
items.summary: Discover and shop from IDEA Mississauga-supported businesses at Sourced in Sauga on Saturday, September 26. Business and innovation | September 11, 2026 IDEA Mississauga invites the community to Sourced in Sauga, a one-day celebration of local entrepreneurship presented in partnership with Square One Shopping Centre. This pop-up shopping experience brings together some of Mississauga’s most innovative entrepreneurs, artisans and small businesses for a day of discovery, connection and community. From childcare services and toy subscriptions to dog perfumes and handcrafted jewellery, there’s something for everyone. More information about how to register and the full list of vendors is available through the registration link on the Sourced in Sauga event page. Browse a diverse selection of locally made products and services, meet the entrepreneurs behind the brands and learn how IDEA Mississauga’s programs have helped support their growth and success. Shoppers will also have the chance to win one of two Square One gift cards valued at $250 each. So whether you’re looking for unique gifts, getting a head start on seasonal shopping, or simply exploring what Mississauga’s business community has to offer, Sourced in Sauga is an opportunity to support local entrepreneurs and discover something new. m. m.

items.title: Can student residences be designed to fight loneliness? U of T Mississauga is finding out
items.summary: UTM’s new 400-bed building is designed to create face-to-face interactions to improve students’ mental health. At the University of Toronto Mississauga campus, student housing is shifting away from traditional apartment-style layouts to a more hostel-like community space. There is an earthlike smell when you enter the New Residence. The new student housing building designed specifically to foster student mental health is nestled among willow and pine trees in a corner of the University of Toronto Mississauga (UTM) campus. The six-storey copper-brown residence building, the campus’s first new residence in nearly 20 years — the last one was built in 2007 — features 400 new beds, with 115 single rooms, 135 double bedrooms and 15 staff bedrooms, all split into 25 pods. Designed by Montgomery Sisam Architects, the idea was to create stronger student communities by shifting away from traditional student housing models that kept them isolated in their rooms. The hope is to counter an epidemic of loneliness and growing anxiety among students, with Canadian youth reporting higher odds of anxiety and mood disorders. “There is so much light coming into this building (and) so much opportunity for connection,” said Tim Fricker, interim dean of student experience and well-being at UTM.

items.title: ROAD CLOSED: Motorcycle crash leads to injuries in Mississauga
items.summary: Two people have been rushed to hospital following a crash between a motorcycle and multiple other vehicles in Mississauga. m. in the area of Dundas Street West and Ninth Line in Mississauga. Police say a motorcycle and three other vehicles were involved in the crash. The motorcyclist and a driver from one of the other vehicles were transported to hospital in non-life threatening condition. No additional details about the victims or their injuries have been disclosed by police. Officers are on the scene and say all lanes have been closed on Ninth Line from Fern Hill School to Dundas Street. Drivers should expect delays and avoid the area if possible. items.title: One of biggest used book sales in Ontario is back in Mississauga
items.summary: Book lovers in Mississauga — and from other places near and far — likely have plans to be in the same spot late next week. The Mississauga Symphony Orchestra’s Giant Used Book Sale, considered among the largest such events in Ontario, returns to the city for a 31st year starting Sept. 17. The four-day sale runs through Sept. 20 and is being held once again on the lower level at Sherwood Village (formerly known at various times over the decades as Sheridan Centre and Sheridan Mall). , just north of the QEW. ” The Mississauga Symphony Orchestra’s Giant Used Book Sale features thousands of fiction and non-fiction titles, vinyl records, CDs, DVDs, puzzles, board games and sheet music. “All items are in excellent condition and listed at unbeatable prices,” book sale organizers said in a news release. Organizers note the book sale is a cash-only event with proceeds going to support the MSO’s annual concert season, the rapidly growing Mississauga Symphony Youth Orchestra and special large-scale projects such as fully-staged opera.

items.title: Police say $15K in stolen goods from across GTA recovered from Brampton home — father, mother, son, son-in-law face charges
items.summary: Peel police say a single theft call in Mississauga in June led investigators to connect the suspects to a series of retail thefts across the region. Peel Regional Police have charged four Brampton residents following an investigation into a series of organized retail thefts across the Greater Toronto Area. Members of a Brampton family face charges following an investigation into a series of organized retail thefts across the Greater Toronto Area. Peel Regional Police said that on June 18 officers responded to a theft at a business near Clayhill Road and Dundas Street in Mississauga. “Through the investigation, detectives identified several suspects and connected them to additional retail theft incidents throughout Peel Region,” police alleged in a Sept. 9 news release. On July 20, police executed a search warrant at a home near Mississauga and Mayfield roads in Brampton and said they recovered about $15,000 worth of property stolen from several retailers. “Officers also seized two vehicles, jewelry and cash in various currencies,” the news release said. Four Brampton residents have been charged.

items.title: Crisis worker details struggle before fatal 2023 fall at Mississauga home
items.summary: Crisis worker Augustine Aigbekaen testified he wasn’t expecting a mental health apprehension — moments later, John Brownlie fell down a flight of stairs. The inquest is expected to conclude Sept. 18. Retired Mississauga schoolteacher John Brownlie, 88, dies in September 2023 following an interaction with a Peel Regional Police officer. This summary was produced using artificial intelligence and reviewed by an editor for accuracy and clarity. A crisis support worker recounted a tense struggle between a Peel police officer and 88-year-old John Brownlie on the second day of an inquest into the Mississauga man’s fatal 2023 fall. Augustine Aigbekaen was a worker with the Crisis Outreach and Support Team (COAST), which pairs plainclothes police officers with community-based crisis workers from the Canadian Mental Health Association (CMHA) to support those with mental health or addiction crises. Brownlie’s wife, Doris, had called a crisis line on Sept. 12, 2023, after he refused to be taken to a doctor. That call led to a visit the same day by crisis support worker Shanjot Singh. Aigbekaen testified on Sept. 9 that Brownlie was identified — on Sept. 13, 2023 — as being “appropriate” for a COAST visit. He noted there was concern about cognitive decline and delusional and paranoid behaviour.

items.title: Mayoral candidates to debate issues impacting businesses in Mississauga
items.summary: Mississauga’s four main mayoral candidates will meet on the debate stage in two weeks in the downtown core to present their plans for addressing key issues impacting the city’s business community. The top four polling candidates — incumbent Carolyn Parrish, former mayor Bonnie Crombie and city councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla — will square off as the Mississauga Board of Trade hosts its 2026 Mississauga Mayoral Debate on Sept. 25 at the Sheridan College Hazel McCallion Campus. m. Theme of the event is “business and leadership,” according to the board of trade, which represents some 1,000 larger businesses in addition to numerous smaller operations across Mississauga. Mayor Carolyn Parrish, at right, and former mayor Bonnie Crombie will debate key Mississauga business issues on Sept. 25. The Mississauga Board of Trade describes the upcoming debate as “an important conversation about Mississauga’s future” and adds it will provide an opportunity “to hear directly from mayoral candidates” as they discuss issues of most importance to city businesses of all sizes. “Whether you’re a business leader, entrepreneur, professional or engaged member of the Mississauga community, this is an opportunity to hear the candidates’ perspectives and learn more about their vision for the city,” MBOT said in an online notice of the debate. In-person attendance is exclusively available to MBOT members, “offering members a unique opportunity to experience the debate live and engage with the discussion in person,” organizers said.

items.title: Controversial condo project deferred in Mississauga
items.summary: A controversial Mississauga condo project has been deferred. Residents came out to oppose the project at 900 Lakeshore Rd. W. in Lorne Park this week. The property is next to Richard’s Memorial Park, currently home to a single-detached house with a pool. The revised plans to build a nine-storey condominium apartment building with 161 units came to the City of Mississauga’s Planning and Development Committee on Sept. 8. After community members made delegations opposing the current plan, the committee voted in favour of deferring the project. The development plans have long been the subject of opposition, with residents holding a rally against the so-called “cruise ship” condo in 2025. While there have been several changes to the plans, including reducing the height and size of the building, there are still many concerns, particularly because the development is next to beloved natural areas. The wetland and natural heritage features will be protected, and water and sewer infrastructure can be made available, Mississauga City Planner Paul Stewart said at the Sept. 8 meeting. The building lot is on a slope, but it will remain stable, Stewart said. However, councillors and residents wanted more details on how the new building would mitigate environmental concerns.
